messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: Javascript engine in knitr
parts:
Hello, just for sharing : http://rpubs.com/stla/72006

Source Rmd :

```{r}
library(knitr)
split_results <- function (x, sep) # function borrowed from runr package
{
    x = strsplit(paste(x, collapse = " "), sep)[[1]]
    res = vector("list", length(x))
    for (i in seq_along(x)) {
        el = gsub("^ +| +$", "", x[i])
        res[[i]] = if (i%%2 == 1)
            structure(list(src = el), class = "source")
        else paste(el, collapse = " ")
    }
    res
}
knit_engines$set(V8 = function(options) {
  code <- as.character(c(options$code))
  output <- ct$eval(code)
  code <- lapply(split_results(code, sep="this_is_a_stupid_string"), function(x) knitr:::wrap.source(x, options))
  if(options$results=="hide") return(code)
  else return(c(code, knitr:::wrap.character(output, options)))
})
```


Load `V8` and define a new context named `ct`:

```{r}
library(V8)
ct <- new_context()
```

Define `x` in Javascript context using the chunk option `engine='V8'`:

```{r, engine='V8'}
var x=[];
x.push([1,2]);
x.push([3,4]);
x.push([5,6]);
JSON.stringify(x)
```

Get `x` in R :

```{r}
( x.in.R <- ct$get("x") )
```

Double `x` in R and assign in Javascript context :

```{r}
ct$assign("double_x", 2*x.in.R)
```

```{r, engine='V8'}
JSON.stringify(double_x);
```

Load a Javascript library :

```{r}
ct$source(system.file("js/underscore.js", package="V8"))
```

```{r, engine='V8'}
JSON.stringify(_.flatten(x))
```

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Javascript engine in knitr
parts:
The random string in runr is used to separate source code from output.
In the case of V8/JavaScript, there is no need to do so, because it is
easy to know which part is source code and which is output in R. (See
what I wrote in the Github issue) In the case of Julia, the source
code and output are mixed on the Julia side, and I will have to split
them after I receive everything back from Julia.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Javascript engine in knitr
parts:
You can send the pull request to the knitr repo instead of runr. I
guess it may take a few rounds of revisions, though. You have to
understand the data structure passed to knitr:::wrap(), i.e. the data
structure returned by evaluate::evaluate(). Then consider what I wrote
here: https://github.com/yihui/runr/issues/11

For the question about the context ct, you can create a default
context, and let users override it via a certain chunk option, e.g.
options$engine.opts$context.

I guess the challenge here is how to make what I'm thinking clear to
you. There are a few technical details that are a bit difficult to
describe (I may be able to write the V8 engine by myself before I'm
able to tell you everything on my mind...), and this feature is not an
urgent one to me.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

>> >> >             structure(list(src = el), class = "source")
>> >> >         else paste(el, collapse = "\n")
>> >> >     }
>> >> >     res
>> >> > }
>> >> > knit_engines$set(V8 = function(options) {
>> >> >   code <- as.character(c(options$code))
>> >> >   output <- ct$eval(code)
>> >> >   code <- lapply(split_results(code, sep="this_is_a_stupid_string"),
>> >> > function(x) knitr:::wrap.source(x, options))
>> >> >   if(options$results=="hide") return(code)
>> >> >   else return(c(code, knitr:::wrap.character(output, options)))
>> >> > })
>> >> > ```
>> >> >
>> >> >
>> >> > Load `V8` and define a new context named `ct`:
>> >> >
>> >> > ```{r}
>> >> > library(V8)
>> >> > ct <- new_context()
>> >> > ```
>> >> >
>> >> > Define `x` in Javascript context using the chunk option
>> >> > `engine='V8'`:
>> >> >
>> >> > ```{r, engine='V8'}
>> >> > var x=[];
>> >> > x.push([1,2]);
>> >> > x.push([3,4]);
>> >> > x.push([5,6]);
>> >> > JSON.stringify(x)
>> >> > ```
>> >> >
>> >> > Get `x` in R :
>> >> >
>> >> > ```{r}
>> >> > ( x.in.R <- ct$get("x") )
>> >> > ```
>> >> >
>> >> > Double `x` in R and assign in Javascript context :
>> >> >
>> >> > ```{r}
>> >> > ct$assign("double_x", 2*x.in.R)
>> >> > ```
>> >> >
>> >> > ```{r, engine='V8'}
>> >> > JSON.stringify(double_x);
>> >> > ```
>> >> >
>> >> > Load a Javascript library :
>> >> >
>> >> > ```{r}
>> >> > ct$source(system.file("js/underscore.js", package="V8"))
>> >> > ```
>> >> >
>> >> > ```{r, engine='V8'}
>> >> > JSON.stringify(_.flatten(x))
>> >> > ```
